content.user_title: Add Structured Logging to Python Apps
content.value_statement: Python services often produce plain text logs that are hard to search and correlate. This skill helps configure structlog for structured JSON logs, context binding, testing, and production-friendly processors.
actual_capabilities: Configure basic structlog loggers and processor chains.
Generate JSON-formatted logs for Python application events.
Bind request and user context to related log messages.
Integrate structlog with the Python standard logging module.
Capture and assert log output in pytest with LogCapture.
Add exception and traceback processors for error logging.
limitations: Provides examples and guidance, not a complete logging platform.
Does not add log shipping, rotation, storage, or alerting.
Requires users to avoid logging credentials, tokens, and personal data.
Examples require a Python application with structlog installed.

use_cases.title: Add Request Context
use_cases.description: Attach request identifiers and user context to logs so related events are easier to trace.

use_cases.title: Prepare Production Logs
use_cases.description: Configure JSON output and efficient processors for log aggregation in production systems.

use_cases.title: Test Logging Behavior
use_cases.description: Use LogCapture to verify log events, fields, and context during automated tests.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to add structlog to a small Python service with console output for local development.

prompt_templates.title: JSON Request Context
prompt_templates.prompt: Configure structlog for a Python web application that emits JSON logs and binds request_id for each request.

prompt_templates.title: Standard Logging Integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Update an existing Python app that uses logging so structlog processors add levels, timestamps, and exception details.

prompt_templates.title: Production And Tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a production structlog configuration with context variables, exception tracebacks, performance considerations, and pytest LogCapture tests.

output_examples.input: I need request tracking in a Python API.
output: A structlog setup using JSON output and context binding.
Request identifiers are attached once and reused across log messages.
Production logs become easier to filter in aggregation tools.

output_examples.input: I want to verify logging in tests.
output: Assertions check event names and expected context fields.
The test keeps logging behavior visible during refactors.

output_examples.input: I need readable development logs and structured production logs.
output: A renderer choice that separates development console output from production JSON output.
Processor order includes level, timestamp, exception formatting, and final rendering.
The configuration is placed at application startup.

best_practices: Configure structlog once during application startup.
Bind stable request context before business logic runs.
Use console rendering locally and JSON rendering in production.
anti_patterns: Logging passwords, tokens, or sensitive personal data.
Reconfiguring structlog inside every request or log call.
Using slow development renderers in high-throughput production paths.

faq.question: What does this skill help configure?
faq.answer: It helps configure structlog for structured Python logging, context binding, JSON output, exceptions, and tests.

faq.question: Does it replace Python standard logging?
faq.answer: No. It can integrate with standard logging and add structured processors around existing loggers.

faq.question: Can it create production JSON logs?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples show JSON rendering and processor chains suitable for log aggregation systems.

faq.question: Can it help with request tracing?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows how to bind request identifiers and user context to related log messages.

faq.question: Does it include log storage or shipping?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on application logging configuration, not storage, transport, rotation, or alerting.

faq.question: How should sensitive data be handled?
faq.answer: Do not log secrets or personal data. Add filtering processors when logs may contain sensitive fields.
